office_does: The sheriff is Okanogan County's chief law enforcement officer, running patrol, investigations, search and rescue, 911 dispatch and the county jail, elected countywide for four years.
race_blurb: Both candidates prefer the Republican Party. Jodie Barcus, appointed sheriff in April 2026 after Paul Budrow resigned, runs on continuity, staffing gains and a jail re-entry program; deputy Gisberth (Giz) Gonzalez says trust in the office has deteriorated and wants incarceration used as a deterrent and contract inmates revived. The ballot carries both the short term and the full term.

candidates.summary: Okanogan County Sheriff since April 2026 (appointed), previously chief criminal deputy and a Colville Tribal Police narcotics officer; first woman to serve as the county's sheriff.
highlights: Appointed sheriff by the county commissioners on March 31, 2026, after serving as chief criminal deputy from 2023 [S5][S6]
Backs diversion, drug court and a jail re-entry program linking inmates to treatment: 'The jail is not a psych ward' [S5][S9]
Priorities include drugs, crimes against children and jail staffing; calls the aging jail the most pressing problem [S7][S9]
Says the office must 'be very budget conscious and stay within our budget' [S7]

experience.basis: Sitting (appointed) sheriff with command experience as chief criminal deputy, though only six months in the top job.

safety.basis: Pairs enforcement priorities (drugs, crimes against children, jail capacity) with explicit support for diversion, drug court and treatment-based re-entry.

spending.basis: Stresses staying within the office's budget, buying used patrol vehicles and treating grants as not 'free money'.

candidates.summary: Okanogan County sheriff's deputy since 2007 (corrections officer, then patrol, Special Response Team and field training officer), running for his first elected office.
highlights: Calls jail staffing 'the number one issue facing the sheriff's office' [S2]
'Incarceration should be used as a deterrent even though there are other alternatives'; blames state laws for 'alternatives to incarceration' [S2]
Says trust in the office 'has deteriorated' and proposes servant leadership and transparency [S1][S2]
Proposes reviving contract inmates for revenue [S1][S2]

experience.basis: Long-serving line deputy with no supervisory or elected record, running as the change candidate against the appointed sheriff.

safety.basis: Wants incarceration used as a deterrent, proactive policing, and criticizes state 'alternatives to incarceration'.

reform.basis: Says trust in the office has deteriorated and attributes staffing problems mainly to leadership; runs on changing the office's leadership.
